title: S. Korea, Japan Have Best Paternity Leave Pay — Study
paragraphs: If you are a new father, where in the world would you get the most money for taking time off work? According to a new study, the answer is South Korea, followed closely by Japan.

The study was carried out by Moorepay, a British company that provides payroll and human resources services. It compared statutory paternity and parental leave, meaning the leave that fathers are guaranteed by law, in countries around the world.

To make the comparison fair, the researchers used a "model father." He was a first-time parent in a two-parent family, working in the private sector. They then calculated how much he would be paid during his leave, based on each country's average income. Finally, they adjusted the amounts to take into account differences in living costs between countries.

South Korea came first in the overall ranking. According to the study, a father there could receive more than 36 million won, worth about $42,800 after adjusting for living costs. South Korea also offers fathers the longest paid parental leave of any country, at 82 weeks, and the longest leave at full pay, at 43.4 weeks.

Japan also scored highly. It offers the second-longest paid parental leave, at 48 weeks, and its total pay was worth about $27,500 after adjusting for living costs. Other countries near the top of the ranking included Luxembourg, Sweden, Norway, Iceland, Denmark and Finland, mostly countries in northern Europe.
However, many other countries offer very little or nothing. Under the study's model, 51 countries, including the United States and New Zealand, have no statutory paid paternity leave at all.

Generous benefits do not always mean that many fathers actually use them. In both countries, relatively few men took leave in the past. However, this is changing. In Japan, for example, more than half of eligible fathers took childcare leave in the 2025 fiscal year, a record high.
